newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia July-Jan budget deficit A$10.16 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia July-Jan budget deficit A$10.16 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the seven months to January, the first seven months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$10.160 billion, compared with A$11.599 billion, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Friday.
The headline balance -- which includes asset sales -- was a A$6.148 billion deficit, compared with a A$6.521 billion deficit for the same period last fiscal year, Fahey said in a statement.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Revenue growth to January was 6.8 percent, compared with estimates in the government's mid-year budget review of 5.8 percent.
Outlays grew 5.7 percent, compared with mid-year budget review projections of 3.8 percent, Fahey said.
Revenue growth was fuelled by a 6.8 percent increase in tax receipts over the same period in 1995/96.
The main increases in spending were in health, social security, and lower state government debt repayments.
The monthly headline balance for January was a A$950 million deficit, compared with a deficit of A$1.214 billion a year earlier.
The underlying balance for the month was a A$1.078 billion deficit, compared with a A$1.271 billion deficit in January 1996.
